subject: Competitive match: tactical pricing structure and integration SLAs
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Larson <emma@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive match: tactical pricing structure and integration SLAs

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table so your procurement and engineering teams can weigh integration risk versus commercial tradeoffs. Attached is a short one-pager (redwood_match_summary.pdf) — highlights below.

- Term: 12 months with optional annual renewal
- Commercial options (pick one):
  1) 18% platform discount year 1 + standard support
  2) $30k migration & integration credit applied on first invoice + 8% platform discount
- SLA commitments: 99.9% regional uptime, 100ms median gen latency target for our recommended small model profile; credit tiers for missed SLAs (pro-rated)
- Integration support: dedicated onboarding engineer for pilot (up to 40 hours), canary rollout assistance, runbook review
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II available on request; we can provide an isolated VPC demo for your infra team

Two quick asks: (1) can you confirm whether the team prefers credits or pure % discount (Brightlane typically prefers credits for migration), and (2) what SLA credit threshold your procurement would expect for a mid-enterprise contract?

If helpful, I can loop in Marcus (cc'd) with a line-by-line economic breakdown. Would love to get a 30-minute sync this week to run through the SLA mechanics and a pilot timeline.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_match_summary.pdf
From: Emma Larson <emma@brightlane.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive match: tactical pricing structure and integration SLAs

Chloe —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few items we need clarified before we escalate to legal/procurement:

- SLA credits: what is the exact credit schedule and how is it calculated (example scenarios would help)
- Support window: do you include weekend/holiday on-call for critical sev1 incidents?
- Data controls: retention, deletion timelines, and can we get a template DPA?
- Egress: any per-GB charges post-migration or included in the plan?

Also attaching a short list of Brightlane security/compliance questions we typically run through (Brightlane_compliance_questions.docx). Procurement prefers a narrower set of commercial options rather than many combinable offers — can you present a single recommended path with fallback?

Procurement contact is procurement@brightlane.com — feel free to include them on the next note.

Emma Larson
VP of Platform, Brightlane
emma@brightlane.com

Attachment: Brightlane_compliance_questions.docx
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Larson <emma@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive match: tactical pricing structure and integration SLAs

Emma —

Appreciate the questions. Quick answers inline and a recommended path at the bottom. Marcus and Priya added for technical/commercial detail.

- SLA credits: Example schedule (pro-rated monthly):
  * <99.9% uptime in region = 5% invoice credit; <99.5% = 10% credit; <99% = 25% credit (applies to affected region and month). We calculate using aggregated healthy-serving time across the host pool.
  * Credits apply as account-level credits on the following invoice, not cash refunds.

- Support window: Standard included support is M-F 6am–6pm PT with 24/7 sev1 on-call escalation (phone + pager) for critical production outages. On-call includes weekend coverage for sev1.

- Data controls/DPA: We have a standard DPA template and redact examples; SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA. Retention/deletion can be configured per-customer; default deletion within 30 days of contract end unless otherwise agreed.

- Egress: No per-GB egress charges for API responses within the included plan; large bulk exports can be agreed as a one-time transfer fee if necessary.

Recommended path (single option):
- Recommended: $30k migration credit + 8% platform discount year 1. Reason: credits defray immediate integration costs and make your first-quarter TCO neutral while still keeping unit economics favorable for Brightlane long-term.

I've attached a simple cost breakdown spreadsheet (match_breakdown.xlsx) that maps the credit vs discount scenarios across your expected monthly token volume.

Next steps: 1) If you agree with the recommended path, we can issue a term sheet for signature and a separate runbook for the pilot; 2) If procurement wants the discount-first approach we can model that as well.

Proposed times for a 30-min sync: Wed 6/9 10:00am PT or Thu 6/10 9:00am PT. Which works for you and procurement?

Best,
Chloe

Attachment: match_breakdown.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Larson <emma@brightlane.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive match: tactical pricing structure and integration SLAs

Emma / team —

Quick technical/commercial note to clarify our delivery commitments if Brightlane picks the credit-led path:

- Migration credit use: credit covers onboarding engineering time, initial model tuning (up to two model variants), and canary rollout support (we'll allocate a dedicated onboarding engineer for up to 40 hours).
- Dedicated infra: we can stand up a logically isolated Dedicated pool for Brightlane on launch month 1 (single-region) to minimize noisy-neighbor risk — this is feasible within the $30k credit in most cases but we can carve out extra run-hours if you need higher isolation SLA.
- Rollout: recommended 3-phase rollout — pilot (2–4 weeks), canary (1 week with 10% traffic), ramp (2–4 weeks). We'll provide runbook steps and rollback triggers in writing.

If procurement is sensitive to credit accounting, a blended option is also possible: $20k credit + 12% discount year 1. Happy to model both in the spreadsheet.

-Marcus
Director, Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Larson <emma@brightlane.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive match: tactical pricing structure and integration SLAs

Chloe / Marcus —

Thanks — the breakdown is helpful. Procurement and engineering prefer the credit-led path (Brightlane historically values explicit migration credits for vendor switch visibility).

Request from procurement: please provide an editable term sheet and a 10-business-day window for redlines. Also can you send the DPA and SOC 2 NDA so we can run a quick legal review?

We'd like to book Wed 6/16 10:00am PT for the pilot kickoff sync — can you confirm availability for your onboarding engineer and an exec sponsor?

Emma
VP of Platform, Brightlane
